research_question: Does the 8–10 week cross-sectional reversal effect strengthen among high-volatility crypto assets and survive realistic perpetual-futures costs?
hypothesis: Recent 8–10 week losers subsequently outperform recent winners, especially among assets with high past volatility, consistent with delayed correction of overshooting in speculative crypto markets.
source_alignment: The source documents Binance USDT cross-sectional reversal over 8–10 week formation windows and reports materially stronger Sharpe when conditioning on high past volatility. This test fixes 8/9/10-week windows before results.
data: Binance USD-M USDT perpetuals, 1h aggregated to complete UTC days.
universe_rule: Every Monday, among causally eligible contracts, retain top 50 by lagged trailing-30-day quote volume; then retain the higher-volatility half by lagged 30-day realized daily-return volatility.

feature.signal: negative cumulative close-to-close return over the formation window ending on the prior completed day
feature.volatility_condition: top 50% within the liquid top-50 universe

portfolio: Equal-weight long loser quintile / short winner quintile within the conditioned universe, 0.5 gross per side.
rebalance: Weekly Monday 00:00 UTC; execute at Monday open and hold to next Monday open.
development_gate: Canonical mean rank IC >0.02 with HAC p<0.05, positive loser-minus-winner spread, canonical net Sharpe >0.70 and total return >0, and >=2/3 formation windows positive.
success_gate: Canonical OOS net Sharpe >1.0; positive at 2x costs; >=2/3 windows positive; 2024 and 2025 non-negative; max drawdown <35%; excluding BTC/ETH positive; excluding strongest contributor positive; one-day delayed execution positive; family and global DSR >=0.95.
